'''Sandra Myrna Díaz''' ''[[ForMemRS]]'' (born in 1961) is an Argentine ecologist and professor of [[ecology]] at the [[National University of Córdoba]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sandra Diaz|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=fPHP7JwAAAAJ&hl=en|access-date=2020-11-12|website=scholar.google.com}}</ref> who has been awarded with the Linnean Medal for her scientific work. She studies the [[Phenotypic trait|functional traits]] of plants and investigates how plants impact the [[ecosystem]].<ref name="Chapin IIIZavaleta2000">{{cite journal|last1=Chapin III|first1=F. Stuart|author-link2=Erika Zavaleta|last2=Zavaleta|first2=Erika S.|last3=Eviner|first3=Valerie T.|last4=Naylor|first4=Rosamond L.|last5=Vitousek|first5=Peter M.|last6=Reynolds|first6=Heather L.|last7=Hooper|first7=David U.|last8=Lavorel|first8=Sandra|author-link8=Sandra Lavorel |last9=Sala|first9=Osvaldo E.|last10=Hobbie|first10=Sarah E.|last11=Mack|first11=Michelle C.|last12=Díaz|first12=Sandra|title=Consequences of changing biodiversity|journal=Nature|volume=405|issue=6783|year=2000|pages=234–242|issn=0028-0836|doi=10.1038/35012241|pmid= 10821284|s2cid=205006508|hdl=11336/37401|hdl-access=free}} {{closed access}}</ref>

Díaz is a senior member of the [[National Scientific and Technical Research Council]] and the [[National Academy of Sciences of Argentina]]. She is one of the 1% most cited scientists in the world.<ref name=gs>{{Google scholar id}}</ref><ref name=high/> She was elected a [[Foreign Member of the Royal Society]] (ForMemRS) in 2019<ref name=formemrs>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/sandra-diaz-14086/|title=Sandra Diaz|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|author=Anon|year=2019|website=royalsociety.org|access-date=20 April 2019}} One or more of the preceding sentences incorporates text from the royalsociety.org website where: {{blockquote|“All text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]].” --{{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161111170346/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/|title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies|date=2016-11-11}}}}</ref> and an international member of the [[American Philosophical Society]] in 2022.<ref name=":4" >[https://www.amphilsoc.org/blog/american-philosophical-society-welcomes-new-members-2022 The American Philosophical Society Welcomes New Members for 2022]</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Díaz was born in [[Bell Ville]] in the province of [[Córdoba, Argentina]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://archivo.lavoz.com.ar/especiales/cordobes07/nota.asp?nota_id=134159|title=LAVOZ.com.ar {{!}} Sandra Díaz|website=Archivo.lavoz.com.ar|access-date=2019-04-20}}</ref> Her parents loved plants and she grew up in a home with big gardens.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last=Trivedi|first=Bijal P.|date=2012|title=Profile of Sandra M. Díaz|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|language=en|volume=109|issue=29|pages=11469–11471|doi=10.1073/pnas.1210043109|issn=0027-8424|pmid=22761316 |pmc=3406846 |bibcode=2012PNAS..10911469T|doi-access=free }}</ref>

Díaz attended the [[National University of Córdoba]] and graduated [[cum laude]] with a biology degree in 1984.<ref name=":0" /> She decided that she wanted to be an environmental scientist, and chose to pursue graduate research. She remained at [[National University of Córdoba]] for her doctoral, earning a PhD in biological sciences in 1989.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://interacademies.org/9836/Professor-Sandra-Diaz|title=Professor Sandra Díaz|website=Iinteracademies.org|access-date=2019-04-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190324131038/https://interacademies.org/9836/Professor-Sandra-Diaz|archive-date=24 March 2019}}</ref> She worked with [[Marcelo Cabido]] and [[Alicia Acosta]] on plant functional traits.<ref name=":0" /> During her [[PhD]] and later research Díaz developed the protocols to support scientists using functional traits to interpret [[ecosystem]]s.<ref name=":0" /> Díaz was a [[fellow]] at [[CONICET]], the center for ecology and natural resources.

==Career and research==
After reading a book by [[J. Philip Grime]] about the connection between plant strategies, ecosystem processes and environmental factors, Díaz applied to work with him in the United Kingdom.<ref name=":0" /> In 1991 Díaz joined the [[University of Sheffield]] as a [[postdoctoral research]] associate.<ref name=":0" />

At Sheffield she studied how [[plant community|plant communities]] respond to increasing quantities of [[carbon dioxide]] (CO<sub>2</sub>). She was the first to demonstrate an important feedback between plants and soil microbes under elevated carbon dioxide. She found that, even in the presence of [[fertilizer]], weedy plants that grow quickly suffer from heightened levels of carbon dioxide.<ref name=":0" /> At the same time, [[microorganism]]s in the soil thrived in high levels of [[carbon dioxide]], indicating that there is a competition between plants and soil for [[nitrogen]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Díaz|first1=S.|last2=Grime|first2=J. P.|last3=Harris|first3=J.|last4=McPherson|first4=E.|date=1993|title=Evidence of a feedback mechanism limiting plant response to elevated carbon dioxide|journal=Nature|volume=364|issue=6438|pages=616–617|doi=10.1038/364616a0|issn=0028-0836|bibcode=1993Natur.364..616D|s2cid=4272738}} {{closed access}}</ref> Diaz also showed that slow-growing plants have a more positive feedback mechanism.<ref name="Cabido"/>

Díaz returned to Argentina in 1993, where she moved back into studying plant traits.<ref name="Cabido">{{Cite journal|last1=Diaz|first1=Sandra|last2=Cabido|first2=Marcelo|date=1997|title=Plant functional types and ecosystem function in relation to global change|journal=Journal of Vegetation Science|volume=8|issue=3|pages=463–474|doi=10.1111/j.1654-1103.1997.tb00842.x|issn=1100-9233|jstor=3237198|bibcode=1997JVegS...8Q.463D }}</ref> She was a principal lead author to the chapter on "Rangelands in a Changing Climate: Impacts, Adaptations, and Mitigation" in the 1995 report of the [[Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change]] (IPCC).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chapter 2: Rangelands in a Changing Climate: Impacts, Adaptations, and Mitigation - AR2 WG2|url=https://www.ipcc.ch/site/assets/uploads/2018/03/ipcc_sar_wg_II_full_report.pdf|access-date=2021-07-30|website=archive.ipcc.ch}}</ref> Díaz founded the Núcleo DiverSus de Investigaciones en Diversidad y Sustentatibilidad.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://www.nucleodiversus.org/index.php?mod=page&id=39|title=Sandra M. Díaz {{!}} DiverSus group|website=Nucleodiversus.org|access-date=2019-04-19}}</ref>

She has played an important role in the development and implementation of functional biodiversity.<ref name=":2" /> As part of CONICET Díaz developed a new methodology to quantify the functional biodiversity of plants.<ref>{{Cite journal |title=Linking functional diversity and social actor strategies in a framework for interdisciplinary analysis of nature's benefits to society |year=2011|pmid=21220325 |pmc=3024663|author=Díaz, Sandra |author2=Quétier, Fabien |author3=Cáceres, Daniel M. |author4=Trainor, Sarah F. |author5=Pérez-Harguindeguy, Natalia |author6=Bret-Harte, M. Syndonia |author7=Finegan, Bryan |author8=Peña-Claros, Marielos |author9=Poorter, Lourens |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|volume=108|issue=3|pages=895–902|oclc=720176072 |doi=10.1073/pnas.1017993108 |doi-access=free }}</ref> This tool allows scientists to evaluate the effect of biodiversity of plants and its impact on ecosystems.  Díaz was the first to provide a global picture of the functional diversity of [[vascular plant]]s. She designed a database of tens of thousands of plants, using contributions of 135 scientists.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=TRY>{{Cite journal |journal=Global Change Biology |volume=17 |issue=9 |date=2011 |pages=2905–2935 |display-authors=13|title=TRY - a global database of plant traits|author1=Kattge, J. |author2=Diaz, S. |author3=Lavorel, S. |author4=Prentice, I.C.|author-link4=Colin She explored functional trait diversity on plots of land, dividing vegetation into separate sections to simulate changes in climate and land use.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Díaz|first1=Sandra|last2=Symstad|first2=Amy J.|last3=Stuart Chapin|first3=F.|last4=Wardle|first4=David A.|last5=Huenneke|first5=Laura F.|date=2003|title=Functional diversity revealed by removal experiments|journal=Trends in Ecology & Evolution|volume=18|issue=3|pages=140–146|doi=10.1016/s0169-5347(03)00007-7|issn=0169-5347|hdl=11336/39091|hdl-access=free}} {{closed access}}</ref> She demonstrated that there exists a tradeoff in plant design between the fast acquisition of resources and the conservation of the resources in tissues.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Diaz|first1=S.|last2=Hodgson|first2=J. Díaz is also interested in the interaction between ecology and the [[social science]]s, and looks at how societies value and support ecosystems<ref name=":0" /> and in the relationship between living plants and people. She published a mechanistic framework for connecting functional diversity in 2007, a paper which would go on to win the ''[[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America]]'' (PNAS) Cozzarelli Prize.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Díaz |first1=Sandra |last2=Lavorel |first2=Sandra |last3=de Bello |first3=Francesco |last4=Quétier |first4=Fabien |last5=Grigulis |first5=Karl |last6=Robson |first6=T. == Other activities ==
In 2023, Díaz was appointed by [[United Nations Secretary General]] [[António Guterres]] to the United Nations' Scientific Advisory Board.<ref>[https://press.un.org/en/2023/sga2223.doc.htm UN Secretary-General Creates Scientific Advisory Board for Independent Advice on Breakthroughs in Science and Technology] [[United Nations]], press release of 3 August 2023.</ref>

== Recognition ==
Díaz was listed as one of the [[Nature's 10|''ten people who mattered in science in 2019'' by the journal Nature]] in their end of year review <ref>{{cite web |title=Nature's 10 |url=https://www.nature.com/immersive/d41586-019-03749-0/index.html |publisher=Nature |access-date=19 December 2019}}</ref> In 2023 she was one of the six women chosen by [[Nature (journal)|Nature]] to comment on their plans for [[International Women's Day]]. The others were [[Gihan Kamel]], [[Martina Anto-Ocrah]], [[Jess Wade]], [[Aster Gebrekirstos]] and [[Tanya Monro]].<ref>{{Cite journal |date=2023-03-08 |title=Celebrate women in science — today, and every day |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=615 |issue=7951 |pages=187 |doi=10.1038/d41586-023-00670-5|pmid=36890375 |bibcode=2023Natur.615..187. |s2cid=257380632 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

=== Awards and honours ===
Díaz' awards and honours include:

*2008 [[Ecological Society of America]] Sustainability Award<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://esa.org/history/sustainability-science-award-2/|title=Sustainability Science Awards – The Ecological Society of America's History and Records|language=en-US|access-date=2019-04-20}}</ref>
*2008 ''[[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America]]'' (PNAS) Cozzarelli Prize<ref name=":3" />
*2009 Elected member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sandra M. Diaz|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/sandra-m-diaz-yvgbva/|access-date=2021-07-30|website=www.nasonline.org}}</ref>
*2012 Inaugural Fellow of the Ecological Society of America<ref>{{Cite web |title=ESA Fellows |url=https://esa.org/about/awards/fellows-program/esa-fellows/ |access-date=2025-08-13 |website=Ecological Society of America}}</ref>
*2013 Platinum [[Konex Award]] in Biology and Ecology<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.geap.com.ar/cisen4/en/program|title=CISEN4|website=Geap.com.ar|access-date=2019-04-20}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Galería de Fotos Premios Konex 2013 - Acto Culminatorio: Ciencia y Tecnología : KONEX DE PLATINO - BIOLOGÍA Y ECOLOGÍA - SANDRA DÍAZ |url=https://www.fundacionkonex.org/f5368-konex-de-platino--biologa-y-ecologa--sandra-daz |website=Fundacion Konex |access-date=26 October 2019}}</ref>
